newsitem.title: ISRAEL: IMF urges early passage of Israel 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: IMF urges early passage of Israel 1997 budget.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund recommended in an interim report on Wednesday that Israel accelerate passage of its 1997 budget to help deal with the imbalance in its fiscal accounts.

The IMF also suggested that budget law "set aside a percentage of planned current expenditures in a special reserve fund that would only be released once the government reported to the Knesset (parliament) at midyear that the fiscal accounts remained on track".

"It is essential that the government fulfil its commitments...Nowhere is this more critical than in the fiscal accounts. The imbalance in these accounts is at the core of the current strains and it is essential that the 2.8 percent of GDP (gross domestic product) overall deficit target be achieved," the report said.

To deal with a widening deficit, the new government has proposed cutting 4.9 billion shekels from the 1997 budget. "The beneficial effects of such a budget will only become apparent gradually, however, unless ways are found to hasten and strengthen its credibility," the report said.

The government also plans to cut its budget deficit as a percentage of GDP gradually until 2001. However, the IMF said: "We are concerned that the targeted declines in the deficit will not be sufficient to generate the domestic savings required to sustain a high rate of investment.
"We would urge more ambitious deficit targets both in the medium term -- say balance by 2001 -- and in any one year if favourable economic development permits."

The IMF also urged a medium-term framework for formulating and implementing monetary policy to target underlying inflation. "We would see merit in a framework that aimed to get underlying inflation down to four percent by 2001, with an intermediate target of being below, say, seven percent in 1998," the IMF said.
